title: Tenant-aware embedding activation and versioned fallback policy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a tenant-aware activation flow for new embedding model variants plus a deterministic versioned fallback policy for reranking endpoints. This ticket defines the runtime changes, rollout controls, telemetry signals, and migration steps to safely onboard models with per-tenant activation windows and automatic downgrades when quality or latency regressions are detected.
background: We frequently add new embedding model variants (quantized, fp16, sparse) and need safer ways to test them in production. Current onboarding uses global canaries which produce noisy signals and blocks teams that need tenant-scoped opt-ins (e.g., enterprise customers on Dedicated). Reranking pipelines require stronger version guarantees because a bad embedding variant can hurt downstream ranking quality considerably.
goals: Support per-tenant activation windows (opt-in by tenant ID or label)
Provide deterministic versioned fallback that maps runtime model failures/quality regressions to stable older variants
Expose rollout controls in Console for staged activation and expiry
Ensure monitoring and automatic rollback triggers for quality (r-precision, MRR), latency, and error-rate regressions
scope: Runtime routing: add tenant-aware selection logic to embedding gateway
Control plane: API to register tenant activation rules and expiry dates
Telemetry: add per-tenant embedding quality metrics and tie to reranking evals
Console: UI controls for enabling/disabling a variant by project/tenant
out_of_scope: Model training or model architecture changes
Large-scale tenant migration (handled by SRE-run migration playbooks)
Changes to embedding storage format (vector proto)
acceptance_criteria: Ability to define an activation rule that targets a tenant or tenant label via API and Console
Requests from targeted tenants are routed to the new variant while others remain on the stable variant
Fallback path: when a variant exceeds latency or error thresholds, traffic for affected tenants switches to the pinned stable variant within configured SLA
Per-tenant quality metrics available in Console (r-precision, mean similarity, sample churn) and surfaced for alerts
End-to-end regression test (simulated workload) demonstrating automatic fallback when quality drops >5% relative to baseline
rollout_strategy: Phase 0: Internal-only activation on staging and canary testing with synthetic rerank prompts
Phase 1: Tenant opt-in alpha (manually enrolled customers) with 1% traffic cap and close telemetry review
Phase 2: Scoped ramp to 10% for selected tenants over 48h with automatic health checks
Phase 3: Default activation (global) if no regressions detected for 14 days
All phases support immediate manual disable and an automatic expiry field on activation rules
canary_criteria: error rate (5xx + model-runtime exceptions) < 0.1% absolute increase
no new class of decoding failures (truncated embeddings, NaN vectors) observed in logs
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-tenant quality vs baseline and traffic percent charts
Alerts: auto-escalate when MRR drop >5% for any tenant for 30m or latency >300ms p95 for 15m
Audit logs: record activation, expiry, and programmatic rollbacks for compliance
migration_steps: 1) Add tenant activation rule API and Console form (feature flag behind embedding_activation_v1)
2) Deploy routing change in embedding gateway behind rollout flag (soft launch in staging)
3) Onboard 2 internal tenants and run synthetic reranker suites for 72h
4) Gradually enroll partner tenants and validate telemetry and logs
5) Remove feature flag and expand to all eligible tenants if stable
rollback_plan: Manual rollback via Console: immediate disable activation rule for tenant(s)
Automatic rollback: system flips traffic to pinned stable variant when canary criteria breached
Post-rollback: create incident report, run deeper offline evaluations, and schedule model revert or fix-release
If global issue: emergency API to pin entire project/region to previous stable variant
